IC1.where: a paragraph of its own at the end of the section, after his J. paragraph ("... it might take years to imagine that correction."), before the heading "How should discipline have been done right?"
IC1.his_before: Whatever the situation was, we will contrast it with the corrected version. For my friend J., whose dad savagely beat him every time he smiled, I'd have the corrected version be, he smiles, and his dad smiles, happy to see him happy. Ok, that one might seem too easy, although for J, it might take years to imagine that correction.
IC1.add: If a memory feels too big to redo on your own, there's an actual clinical therapy for that, called [Imagery Rescripting](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/201523223/imagery-rescripting), which I only found out about after I wrote this section. The therapist has you picture them stepping into the memory as the adult you needed, until you learn to be that adult yourself.

IC2.where: a paragraph of its own at the end of the section, after his "I'd ask for a chronic pain specialist ..." paragraph, before the heading "Listen To Your Body, Or Else!"
IC2.his_before: I'd ask for a chronic pain specialist and a written plan for the flare-ups you can see coming, including the new or severe signs that mean you go to the ER right away, but don't let amelioration of symptoms be the end of the investigation.
IC2.add: While the investigation goes on, if the tests keep coming back normal, I'd also look into two talk therapies that treat the pain as real: Pain Reprocessing Therapy and Emotional Awareness and Expression Therapy. So far they've mostly been tested on chronic back pain and other muscle and joint pain, where they helped most of the people who got them, so I can't say how they'd do for attacks like these (more on both in [my somatic guide](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/201523223/pain-that-wont-quit)).
